r2-observability-1.summary: Ledger-db experienced a severe lock contention and connection saturation issue starting at 13:05, triggered by a daily reconciliation cron job acquiring a table-level lock on ledger_entries at 13:04. This caused widespread statement timeouts, connection pile-ups, and upstream latency spikes in ledger-service and payments-api.

findings.statement: At 2026-10-17T13:04:02, ledger-db started a cron job reconcile_daily which executed LOCK TABLE ledger_entries IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE.
Ledger-db latency_p99_ms showed an upward anomaly starting at 13:05, jumping from ~15 ms to a peak of 10527.28 ms.
Ledger-db active connections showed an upward anomaly starting at 13:05, surging from ~45 to ~180 active connections.
Ledger-db CPU utilization dropped from ~41% to ~19% starting at 13:05 due to processes blocking on table locks rather than performing active computations.
Starting at 13:05, ledger-db logged continuous warnings of processes waiting for RowExclusiveLock on the ledger_entries relation.
Ledger-db disk usage, memory percentage, RPS, and general error rate metrics remained stable without anomalies during the incident window.

hypotheses.title: Daily reconciliation cron job table lock contention on ledger-db
hypotheses.mechanism: At 2026-10-17T13:04:02, the daily reconciliation cron job executed LOCK TABLE ledger_entries IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE (log-00400). This table-level lock conflicted with incoming transactional INSERT INTO ledger_entries statements, causing hundreds of backend processes to wait for RowExclusiveLock starting at 13:05 (log-00414). As connections piled up (metric:ledger-db:connections_active surging from ~45 to ~180) and query latency spiked (metric:ledger-db:latency_p99_ms jumping to over 10 seconds), concurrent ledger writes hit the 10-second statement timeout (log-00445), cascading upstream into ledger-service and payments-api error and latency anomalies at 13:06 (metric:payments-api:error_rate_pct, metric:ledger-service:error_rate_pct).

supporting.note: ledger-db cron job executed LOCK TABLE ledger_entries at 13:04:02, directly preceding the anomaly.
Continuous warnings starting at 13:05 for processes waiting for RowExclusiveLock on ledger_entries.
Ledger-db latency spiked upward starting at 13:05.
Ledger-db active connections surged starting at 13:05.
Ledger-service statements timed out on INSERT INTO ledger_entries starting at 13:06.

assumptions: The reconcile_daily cron job holds the table lock for the duration of the reconciliation process, blocking concurrent writes.

hypotheses.title: Payments-api logging configuration change causing thread pool or serialization overhead
hypotheses.mechanism: The config change chg-9660 at 13:02 changing logging.ledger_client from INFO to DEBUG caused excessive synchronous logging overhead, leading to timeouts when calling downstream services.

supporting.note: Config change on payments-api at 13:02 setting ledger client logging to DEBUG.

contradicting.note: Actual failures are database statement timeouts inside ledger-db and ledger-service, not client-side formatting delays.
ledger-db explicitly started its blocking table lock at 13:04, establishing an independent database-side cause.

assumptions: Verbose logging somehow triggers database-side query locks.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: With ledger-db logs (log-00400, log-00414) and metrics now fully retrieved, the causal chain is completely verified. At 13:04:02, ledger-db executed LOCK TABLE ledger_entries IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE. At 13:05, connections surged, p99 latency spiked, and processes began waiting on locks. At 13:06, upstream writes hit the 10-second statement timeout, causing error rate and latency spikes in ledger-service and payments-api. The payments-api config change (chg-9660) is purely coincidental.
